title: SADC Formally Endorses Africa Forward Summit Nairobi Declaration Digital Transformation Agenda
detail: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) issued a formal post-summit statement on May 14, 2026 confirming its participation in the Africa Forward Summit and endorsement of the Nairobi Declaration's digital transformation agenda. SADC's endorsement brings the combined population of its 16 member states — covering over 350 million people across Southern Africa — under the declaration's commitments on broadband investment, regional data centers, and digital skills training. SADC's statement particularly emphasized the data sovereignty elements of the declaration, noting that African nations need not choose between connectivity and data rights, and that the declaration's cloud and data center investment framework supports both goals. The endorsement signals a broadening of the Africa Forward Summit's political reach beyond the East African and West African nations initially at the negotiating table.

title: SpaceX Targets May 19 for Starship Version 3 Debut — A Key Milestone for Next-Generation Starlink Constellation Capacity
detail: SpaceX announced on May 12–14, 2026 that it is targeting no earlier than May 19 for the debut of Starship Version 3 and the new Launch Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas. While primarily an infrastructure test, Starship V3 carries direct strategic significance for digital inclusion: Starship is the planned heavy-lift vehicle for deploying the next-generation Starlink V3 constellation, which will operate at 340–360 km altitude with massively increased capacity and direct-to-cell capabilities at scale. The Starship V3 design incorporates upgraded Raptor 3 engines and a longer payload bay capable of carrying up to 120 Starlink V3 satellites per launch — compared to ~22 V1.5 satellites per Falcon 9. A successful debut would dramatically accelerate the timeline for Starlink's capacity expansion in underserved regions, particularly Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and rural Latin America. SpaceNews and Spaceflight Now reported the announcement, with space analysts noting the new Launch Pad 2 enables back-to-back launches within weeks.
